hints: Focus on what hot, concentrated $\text{MnO}_4^-$ does to a C=C bond, it cleaves it completely and oxidises each end.
Remember the pattern, $\text{R-CH}=$ gives a carboxylic acid $\text{R-COOH}$, while $\text{R}_2\text{C}=$ gives a ketone, not an acid.
To get two different acids you need both C atoms of the double bond to have one H each, with different alkyl groups attached.
walkthrough:
**Recall the cleavage rule**

Hot, concentrated, acidified manganate(VII) breaks the C=C bond. Each alkene carbon is oxidised separately.

$$\text{R-CH=CH-R'} \rightarrow \text{R-COOH} + \text{R'-COOH}$$
$$\text{R-CH=C(R')}_2 \rightarrow \text{R-COOH} + \text{ketone}$$

**Identify what each alkene needs**

For two carboxylic acids, both carbons must be of the form $\text{-CH=}$. That means a disubstituted alkene $\text{R-CH=CH-R'}$.

If one carbon has no H, you get a ketone instead. If the molecule is symmetrical, you get the same acid twice.

**Apply to the four structures**

Compound B is $\text{CH}_3\text{-CH=CH-CH(CH}_3)_2$, which is 4-methylpent-2-ene. Both double bond carbons have one H.

Cleavage gives:
$$\text{CH}_3\text{-CH=} \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{COOH}$$
$$(\text{CH}_3)_2\text{CH-CH=} \rightarrow (\text{CH}_3)_2\text{CH-COOH}$$
Two different acids, ethanoic acid and 2-methylpropanoic acid.

options.A: A is $\text{CH}_3\text{-CH=C(CH}_3\text{)-CH(CH}_3)_2$, a trisubstituted alkene. The left $\text{CH}$ gives $\text{CH}_3\text{COOH}$ but the right $\text{C}$ has no H so gives a ketone, $(\text{CH}_3)_2\text{CH-CO-CH}_3$. One acid plus one ketone, not two acids.
options.B: B is $\text{CH}_3\text{-CH=CH-CH(CH}_3)_2$. Both alkene carbons are $\text{CH}$ groups with different R groups. Cleavage gives $\text{CH}_3\text{COOH}$ and $(\text{CH}_3)_2\text{CH-COOH}$, two different carboxylic acids.
options.C: C is cyclohexene. Cleavage opens the ring at the double bond to give a single dicarboxylic acid, $\text{HOOC-(CH}_2)_4\text{-COOH}$ (hexanedioic acid). It is one compound containing two acid groups, not two different acids.
options.D: D is $(\text{CH}_3)_2\text{CH-CH=CH-CH(CH}_3)_2$, a symmetrical trans alkene. Both ends are $\text{CH}$ so both give acids, but because the two R groups are identical, you get two molecules of the same acid, $(\text{CH}_3)_2\text{CH-COOH}$.
